title.narrative: Managing integrated TB/HIV response in Papua New Guinea - Papua New Guinea (01-Jan-2025-31-Dec-2026)

description.narrative: Papua New Guinea, TB/HIV, World Vision (PNG) Trust (WV Papua New Guinea)This program has the following goals: Transmission of STIs and HIV is interrupted through targeted access to comprehensive, combination prevention. Effective STI management, early diagnosis, treatment initiation and tailored retention. An enabling environment for universal access to STI and HIV prevention and continuum of care. Reduction in number of TB deaths in 2027 by 50% compared to what was reported in 2015. Reduction in TB incidence rate in 2027 by 20% compared to what was reported in 2015. Proportion of TB affected families facing catastrophic cost reduced to less than 30%. Effective and efficient national HIV & TB programs are enabled by strong coordination, robust systems and a supportive environment for service access. The objectives of this program are: By 2028, 75% of young people will have received STI and HIV prevention information and education through a general community prevention program.. By 2028, 60% of key and priority populations and their partners will have been provided with targeted STI & HIV behaviour change communication and resources. By 2028, 30% of HIV key populations will have access to education and resources that promote safety and wellbeing whilst addressing drivers of STIs and HIV. By 2028, 75% of pregnant women will have clear paths to STI management and HIV testing, treatment, and care as part of the National Package of Services.. By 2028, implement and scale up new approaches, technologies, and medicines to enhance the provision of quality services across the continuum of care for STIs and HIV, ensuring comprehensive, accessible, and effective treatment and prevention strategies.. By 2028, key populations and PLHIV have access to supportive laws and policies, measures to minimize stigma and discrimination, discrimination, legal and complaints services and education on rights for key and priority populations, including PLHIV. By 2027, to have achieved treatment success rate of at least 85% for all forms of TB. By 2027, at least 90% of people with TB provided with universal drug susceptible tests. By 2027, at least 90% of patients with TB tested and know their HIV status. By 2027, the technical and managerial capacities of the tuberculosis program at the national, regional, provincial and district levels for the provision of quality TB services are strengthened.. By 2027, Strong leadership and governance are in place to enable effective and efficient provincial HIV & TB responses. By 2027, robust, data-focused system strengthening are in place to support decentralised HIV & TB programming
